**3.1 Background**

Acme Logistics is planning to modernize its transportation management landscape by deploying SAP S/4HANA Transportation Management and integrating it in real time with its existing Manhattan Warehouse Management System through SAP Cloud Integration middleware. This target-state approach replaces the current legacy nightly batch feed and is intended to improve the timeliness, continuity, and reliability of data exchange between transportation and warehouse operations.

At present, the legacy batch-based integration model introduces dependency on scheduled overnight processing, which can limit operational responsiveness and delay visibility across connected logistics processes. Acme Logistics is therefore pursuing a more integrated, real-time operating model to support improved coordination between systems and business functions.

The business driver for this engagement is to transition from a delayed, batch-oriented interface pattern to a real-time, middleware-enabled architecture that better supports operational decision-making, process synchronization, and future scalability within Acme Logistics' logistics technology landscape.

**3.2 Objectives**

- Deploy SAP S/4HANA TM for Acme Logistics as the target transportation management platform.
- Enable real-time integration between SAP S/4HANA TM and the existing Manhattan WMS.
- Use SAP Cloud Integration middleware as the integration layer between the connected applications.
- Replace the legacy nightly batch feed with a real-time integration approach.
- Improve cross-system data timeliness and operational process alignment across transportation and warehouse functions.
- `<CONFIRM: additional business objectives, success measures, and scope outcomes to be achieved through this engagement>`

**3.3 Indicative To-Be Process Flow**

In the target-state process, SAP S/4HANA TM will serve as the transportation management platform and will exchange data in real time with Manhattan WMS through SAP Cloud Integration middleware. Rather than relying on a nightly batch interface, relevant transportation and warehouse transactions, events, or status updates will flow through the middleware layer as they occur, enabling more current information sharing across systems.

At a high level, the indicative to-be flow is as follows:

- Business transactions and logistics updates originate in SAP S/4HANA TM and/or Manhattan WMS.
- SAP Cloud Integration receives, transforms, and routes the required messages between the systems.
- Manhattan WMS and SAP S/4HANA TM exchange data in real time through the middleware layer.
- The legacy nightly batch feed is retired as part of the target-state integration model.

The proposed solution architecture for this engagement is based on SAP S/4HANA Transportation Management serving as the target transportation management platform for Acme Logistics, with real-time integration established between SAP S/4HANA TM and the existing Manhattan Warehouse Management System through SAP Cloud Integration middleware. This architecture is intended to replace the current legacy nightly batch feed with a more current, event-driven integration model that supports improved timeliness, continuity, and operational alignment across transportation and warehouse processes.

Under the target-state architecture, SAP S/4HANA TM and Manhattan WMS will exchange relevant business transactions, status updates, and logistics data through SAP Cloud Integration, which will act as the middleware layer for message receipt, transformation, routing, and controlled handoff between the connected applications. This architecture is designed to reduce dependency on scheduled batch processing and to support a more responsive operating model across Acme Logistics' logistics technology landscape.

The deployment model for this engagement is based on implementation of SAP S/4HANA TM as the target-state transportation management solution integrated with the existing Manhattan WMS environment. SAP Cloud Integration will be used as the integration layer between the systems in scope. `<TECH TEAM: confirm hosting/deployment model for SAP S/4HANA TM, SAP Cloud Integration tenant landscape, environment strategy across development/test/production, network/connectivity design, interface security design, and production support model>`

In addition to the core SAP S/4HANA TM and Manhattan WMS integration pattern, the architecture includes an interface between Project44 and SAP S/4HANA TM to support the carrier rate engine integration described in scope. `<TECH TEAM: confirm the end-to-end architecture for the Project44 interface, including whether SAP Cloud Integration is used, applicable message flows, triggering events, protocol standards, and exception-handling design>`

The target architecture assumes retirement of the legacy nightly batch feed as part of the transition to the real-time integration model. Any interim coexistence period, fallback mechanism, cutover dependency, or phased decommissioning requirement for the legacy batch interface shall be confirmed during detailed design and incorporated into the final implementation architecture. `<CONFIRM: whether legacy nightly batch feed decommissioning occurs at go-live, during phased transition, or after a defined stabilization period>`

The change-governance structure for the proposed architecture shall operate through formal project governance, solution design review, and approved change control procedures. Architectural decisions affecting scope, interfaces, environments, security controls, deployment approach, custom developments, or non-functional requirements shall be documented, reviewed by authorized project stakeholders, and approved before implementation. Any change that affects commercial terms, delivery timelines, integration volume, or agreed scope boundaries shall be managed through the Change Management Process defined in this SOW. `<CONFIRM: named architecture approvers, design authority/forum, review cadence, and client sign-off process for architecture and integration changes>`

The detailed technical architecture, including system landscape, integration patterns, message specifications, security controls, monitoring approach, and non-functional design requirements, will be finalized during the design phase based on confirmed business, application, and technical requirements. `<TECH TEAM: insert approved architecture diagram showing SAP S/4HANA TM ↔ SAP Cloud Integration ↔ Manhattan WMS real-time integration, Project44 interface architecture, and retirement of the nightly batch feed>`
